Heroes

Source of truth: Assets/Resources/Content/heroes.json (six heroes, all 5-star, all fusable). Aspect-fit notes cross-checked against DESIGN-ASPECTS.md section 3 and DESIGN-WORLD.md. See Aspects for what each aspect's mechanic actually does.

Orrin Kaal — Bulwark of Ash

Role: Bulwark · Aspect: Lumen (relabelled from Ember — see below) · Starting hero

HP 2600, Attack 105, Defense 130, Speed 88, Crit 8%/1.5×, Effect Hit 5%, Effect Resist 20%.

  • Basic — Ashen Cleave: damage to the nearest foe.
  • Active — Cinderguard: Shield on self (22% max HP) + self-Taunt for 2 turns + AllEnemies damage + 70%-chance Burn.
  • Passive — Emberskin: below 50% HP, once per battle, +45% Guard for the rest of the fight.

Aspect fit: originally labelled Ember despite a kit that is Shield/Taunt/DefenseUp — Lumen's rule, verbatim, three times over. Relabelled to Lumen, confirmed in this file ("aspect": "Lumen"). His name, title, lore, and fire-red visual colour were kept deliberately — the fiction explains it as "the ash is where he was, not what he believed" (he held the Cinder Gate, which is in the Ember-ruled Ash Marches). The Taunt line on Cinderguard is now technically redundant, since Lumen's targeting override already routes single-target hits to him with or without it — left in place as orphaned-but-harmless content. He is currently the only Lumen unit in the game on either side of the field.

Kalyx Emberwright — Bloom of Cinders

Role: Breaker · Aspect: Ember · Starting hero

HP 1450, Attack 186, Defense 62, Speed 96, Crit 15%/1.6×, Effect Hit 10%, Effect Resist 5%.

  • Basic — Emberlash: damage to the nearest foe.
  • Active — Cinder Bloom: AllEnemies damage + 85%-chance Burn.
  • Passive: null — no passive in this file.

Aspect fit: clean Ember fit on his active. The JSON confirms his old passive Kindling (+30% damage vs. burning targets) has been removed entirely — the doc flagged it as exactly the flat-percentage stat stick the no-percentage design rule forbids, and it's gone from this file (passive is null), consistent with DESIGN-ASPECTS section 3's call to cut it in favour of the Burn-stacking mechanic doing the same job as a rule instead of a number.

Wren Ilyra — Keeper of the Green Hour

Role: Mender · Aspect: Verdant · Starting hero

HP 1600, Attack 140, Defense 70, Speed 102, Crit 10%/1.5×, Effect Hit 0%, Effect Resist 10%.

  • Basic — Thornspark: damage to the nearest foe.
  • Active — Verdant Tide: Heal AllAllies + Cleanse one affliction.
  • Passive — Rootbound: at battle start, once, Shield on AllAllies worth 9% of Wren's HP.

Aspect fit: flagged as half mismatched. The Heal is Verdant, but the Cleanse is anti-Umbra and Rootbound's Shield is Lumen's rule — two of her three moving parts belong to other aspects. No fix has been made or decided for this; she's called out explicitly as a healer with a protection kit stapled on, and reads as split across colours now that Lumen exists as a real rule.

Ryn Solvarr — Stormlance

Role: Striker · Aspect: Gale · Not a starting hero

HP 1500, Attack 205, Defense 66, Speed 118, Crit 20%/1.7×, Effect Hit 5%, Effect Resist 5%.

  • Basic — Lance Jab: damage to the lowest-HP enemy.
  • Active — Piercing Gale: heavy damage to the lowest-HP enemy + 90%-chance DefenseDown.
  • Passive — Follow-Through: confirmed in this file to trigger on OnKill, granting flat 22 energy.

Aspect fit: her LowestHpEnemy targeting is a clean Gale finisher pattern. Her passive was originally OnCriticalHit — a Tide-shaped trigger (crit-triggered payout) on a Gale hero, called out as the single clearest cross-wiring in the original roster. Fixed: the trigger in this file is now OnKill, matching Gale's "acts again on a kill" identity. Note per the docs: the effect is still EnergyGain, which is Tide's verb, not Gale's — the trigger changed but the payout still doesn't fully match Gale's own vocabulary.

Maeve Corrin — Cadence of the Deep

Role: Warden · Aspect: Tide · Not a starting hero

HP 1700, Attack 148, Defense 82, Speed 108, Crit 12%/1.5×, Effect Hit 0%, Effect Resist 12%.

  • Basic — Tideprod: damage to the nearest foe.
  • Active — Tidal Cadence: AttackUp + Focus + 25 flat energy to AllAllies.
  • Passive — Rising Chorus: every one of Maeve's turns, +8 energy to AllAllies.

Aspect fit: the roster's one clean fit from the start — her entire kit is about other units' cast timing, which is exactly Tide's "redirects" identity. She's also called out as the hero who most obviously wasted the mechanic before Tide's energy-overflow redirect existed — with Rising Chorus ticking every turn, a line sitting near full energy used to throw away most of what she produced.

Nyx Serrow — The Quiet Verdict

Role: Stalker · Aspect: Umbra · Not a starting hero

HP 1420, Attack 227, Defense 58, Speed 126, Crit 28%/1.85×, Effect Hit 35%, Effect Resist 0%.

  • Basic — Hollow Cut: damage to the highest-Attack enemy.
  • Active — Umbral Step: two hits on the highest-Attack enemy.
  • Passive — Hollowing: confirmed in this file, name matches — fires after her basic attack, applies 22% DefenseDown to her last target.

Aspect fit: fits well — "pick the enemy that matters and subtract it" is Umbra's identity written down. Her passive's name was originally Shadowmark, which the World doc flagged as a naming collision (marking is Lumen's verb under the fiction, not Umbra's) — fixed, confirmed renamed to Hollowing in this file, an established Umbra word elsewhere in the content (hollow_husk, Hollow Cut). One remaining stray, not fixed: Umbral Step's effects in this file don't show a Focus line in the raw JSON read for this page, but the doc calls out a Focus self-buff (crit chance, which is Gale's axis) as the one line of her kit that would logically move if fully un-cross-wired — worth re-checking against the live file if this matters for a balance pass, since it wasn't visible as an effect entry in the current active.effects array.

Also notable: her chance on Hollowing is unauthored (defaults to 1.0, unconditional) — flagged in DESIGN-COMBAT-STATS.md as the one place in shipped content where adding the Effect Hit/Resist roll actually changes the RNG draw count, and as an example of a "specialist" identity that worked only because a JSON field was missing rather than because she was actually built to be good at it.

Roster-wide aspect distribution

Ember 1 (Kalyx), Verdant 1 (Wren), Gale 1 (Ryn), Tide 1 (Maeve), Umbra 1 (Nyx), Lumen 1 (Orrin) — now one hero per aspect, following Orrin's relabel. Before the relabel it was Ember 2 / Lumen 0.
